text:
The Hutson name already meant something in Montreal. Now Washington has its own. Cole Hutson, Lane's younger brother and a second-round pick in 2024, has five goals and 12 points in 17 games, including the overtime winner in Ottawa on Tuesday, and he's playing 19:23 a night, up to about 20 minutes lately.

Defensemen picked where he was usually manage about 0.21 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.71. Our wins-added measure ranks him 51st of 522 skaters.

Now the honest part. He's scoring on 14.3% of his shots, more than double the league rate for defensemen and well above our range for him, and the Capitals have scored five more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. Both numbers usually come down. At five-on-five, Washington's share of expected goals (the quality of chances) is about the same with him as without him: good for a 20-year-old, not yet a driver.

What's real is the passing. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has a third of his setups going across the royal road, more than double a typical defenseman, though that's from only six tracked games.
